exceptions.reason: Next 14.2.35 was locked at the PR-01 base. npm proposes a major framework change, which requires App Router and production-build regression work in PR-02.
exceptions.mitigation: Authentication restricts application routes, but no compensating control is claimed to eliminate the framework-level RSC denial-of-service risk.

exceptions.reason: This Server Components denial-of-service advisory affects the locked framework version. The required major Next.js evaluation is isolated to PR-02.
exceptions.mitigation: Protected routes reduce anonymous product access, but this is not considered remediation for a framework parser/resource-exhaustion finding.

exceptions.reason: The finding applies to the existing Next.js version. A framework upgrade plus App Router regression testing is outside the no-upgrade scope of this continuation and is assigned to PR-02.
exceptions.mitigation: No code-level mitigation is claimed; the exception is deliberately short-lived and exact-version bound.

exceptions.reason: The vulnerable Next.js version predates PR-01. Its coordinated upgrade is deferred to PR-02 because it is a framework-level dependency change.
exceptions.mitigation: No custom Node server or WebSocket Upgrade handler is present in this repository, so the advisory's documented application condition was not identified; this is not a version fix.

exceptions.reason: The installed framework version is in the advisory range. Upgrading Next.js is deferred to the dedicated dependency-remediation PR.
exceptions.mitigation: The application uses App Router and no Pages Router i18n configuration was found, so the advisory's documented condition is absent from the checked tree; the package remains vulnerable by version.

exceptions.reason: Server Actions are used, so this finding requires framework remediation. That dependency change and its regressions belong in PR-02, not this gate-only continuation.
exceptions.mitigation: Sensitive Server Actions require an admin guard first, but authorization does not eliminate the framework-level denial-of-service condition.

exceptions.reason: The locked Next.js release is affected by version. Framework remediation is deferred to PR-02 for a separately reviewable upgrade.
exceptions.mitigation: The repository has no custom Node server, which is the advisory's documented execution condition; no claim is made that this fixes the affected dependency.

exceptions.reason: This advisory is present on the PR-01 base framework version. The Next.js upgrade is reserved for PR-02 to keep this continuation free of product/runtime changes.
exceptions.mitigation: No Next.js rewrites configuration was found in the checked tree, so the documented attacker-controlled rewrite path is not configured; the version finding remains open.

exceptions.reason: The affected PostCSS copy is nested under Next.js and existed at the PR-01 base. Resolution must be evaluated with the framework lock graph in PR-02.
exceptions.mitigation: PostCSS is used for repository-controlled build inputs; no runtime path parsing attacker-supplied CSS was identified. This reduces observed exposure but is not remediation.

exceptions.reason: The vulnerable nested PostCSS version is part of the existing Next.js graph. Its safe override or framework upgrade requires dependency testing in PR-02.
exceptions.mitigation: Build CSS is repository controlled and no runtime untrusted CSS parser was identified; the exact vulnerable version is still recorded and time-limited.

exceptions.reason: The package is inherited through Puppeteer's browser installer. Puppeteer remediation must preserve Chromium/PDF behavior and is therefore isolated to PR-02.
exceptions.mitigation: CI disables Puppeteer's browser download. The package remains in the production lock tree, so the exception does not claim the install-time path is universally absent.

exceptions.reason: The affected glob copy belongs to the Next-aligned ESLint toolchain. Updating eslint-config-next with the framework is deferred to PR-02 to avoid a broad tooling upgrade here.
exceptions.mitigation: CI invokes Next lint and never invokes glob's -c/--cmd option with attacker-controlled patterns; this is dev-only exposure, not a dependency fix.

exceptions.reason: Advisory published after PR-01 acceptance against the locked Next 14.2.35. Remediation is the PR-02 major framework upgrade already scheduled for the rest of the Next findings; same deadline applies.
exceptions.mitigation: All application routes except /login and /api/auth sit behind the authentication middleware; no compensating control is claimed to eliminate the framework-level risk.

exceptions.reason: Advisory published after PR-01 acceptance against the locked Next 14.2.35. Remediation is the PR-02 major framework upgrade already scheduled for the rest of the Next findings; same deadline applies.
exceptions.mitigation: All application routes except /login and /api/auth sit behind the authentication middleware; no compensating control is claimed to eliminate the framework-level risk.

exceptions.reason: Advisory published after PR-01 acceptance against the Puppeteer dependency chain. Remediation is the PR-02 Puppeteer 25 major upgrade, same deadline as the existing extract-zip finding.
exceptions.mitigation: extract-zip only runs if Puppeteer downloads a browser at install time; on Railway the Nix chromium is used and the download path is disabled (PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD). No claim is made for other environments.
